lines: Stay off the rows if you can. The crops remember boots.
Give the fields room. Farming works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the fields. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the fields, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Mind the rows. I just convinced them to behave.
Hello. If this is about trampling crops, choose your words carefully.
You caught me with dirt on my hands and work on my mind.
The fields can wait a breath. What do you need?
Step where the path is. The soil and I both appreciate it.
Morning. The crops are judging the weather and so am I.
I have a moment before the next chore notices me.
Come by the fence, not through the wheat.
Good to see you arriving without a herd behind you.
The day is growing whether I am ready or not.
Speak up. The wind has been answering for people all morning.
Hello there. If you brought rain, please be specific about how much.
I was counting seedlings. Try not to distract me into starting over.
Stand clear of the compost and we can talk like civilized folk.
You have my attention until the field steals it back.
